# beowulf-fitt-42 — reviewer pass 2

Every parse in `gloss.json` (91 novel forms, 13 broadened before this pass, 18 after) and every known form occurring in the part checked against its line. Build not run.

## Text changes (line/form · field · severity · what was wrong · what was done)

- 3074 · i · medium · "He had not been keen" turned Næs hē (simple past, as in l "was he") into a pluperfect; "looked ... to the favour" is not gescēawian "beheld" and l has "beheld". Done: "He was not keen on gold; earlier he had more readily beheld the favour of the owner."
- 3079 · i · medium · Pass 1's "by any counsel" still made rǣd ǣnigne the means; l and the note have it as the thing taught (gelǣran takes person and thing). Done: "We could not teach our dear lord ... any counsel by which he would leave the guardian of the gold unchallenged and let him lie ...".
- 3076 · n · medium · Cited the father's names as Wēoxstān 2602, Wēohstān 2862, Wīhstān 2906; line 2906 is "Wīglāf siteð" and has no such form (the forms are Wēoxstānes 2602, Wēohstānes 2862, Wīhstānes 2752, 2907). Done: citations corrected to the genitives actually printed (2752).
- 3087 · n · low · "as at 2956": eorðweall stands at 2957 in the source. Done: corrected.
- 3101 · n · low · "the word being absent from the manuscript" (sīðe) and "the word breaks off in the manuscript" (searo[gimma]) are not in the packet's apparatus; brackets mean only Klaeber's addition. Done: both claims removed; note now says '-gimma' is Klaeber's supply, taken from Bugge and four editors.
- 3101 · l · low · l left the bracketed word [sīðe] unmarked, while 3085 brackets [the man] and fitt-40 brackets [for birds]. Done: "a second [time]".
- 3110 · l · low · boldāgendra is a genitive plural in apposition to hæleða; l gave a bare "house-owners" and the note says "of house-owners". Done: "of the heroes, of house-owners".
- 3120 · l · low · "eight in number he went" does not show eahta sum (sum + genitive plural, "one of eight"), which the note explains. Done: "one of eight he went in under the hostile roof".
- 3131 · i · low · i put "that worm" for wyrm, but the house table sets wyrm = "dragon" in i and dracan is already "dragon" in the same clause. Done: apposition dropped in i ("The dragon too they pushed over the cliff"); l and n keep dracan/wyrm both.

- 3079 · i · "our dear lord" (OE has only lēofne þēoden) — kept; reading as the speaker's lord is the context and l has "beloved prince".

- 3114 · n · "scōc" glossed "speed" — kept; lexicon sense, l and i both say "flew".

- 3069 · i · "foul evils" for wommum — kept (pass 1 refusal stands).
- 3058 · n · "plundered" as the gloss of gehȳðde — kept; gehȳðan is the lexicon verb of hȳð "plunder".
- 3107/3105 · geferian as continuing uton — kept; flagged as a guess.
- All italic-letter claims (3060, 3073, 3078, 3084, 3134, 3135) and apparatus attributions re-checked against the packet; the dot-under-vowel explanation is not needed (no dotted vowel in the part); line cross-references 340, 358, 1412, 2524, 2580, 2631, 2602, 2752, 2756, 2802–2805, 3052 checked against the source.

## Gloss changes (form · field · severity · what was wrong · what was done)

- scēawiað · entry · medium · parsed "2nd plural present subjunctive or indicative"; -iað is indicative (a subjunctive would be scēawien). Done: "2nd plural present indicative".
- wēg · entry · medium · first reading called wēg "object of niman"; in lēton wēg niman it is the accusative subject of niman (the wave takes the keeper), as note, l and i read it. Done: "subject of niman after lēton"; second reading keeps "object of niman".
- folcāgende · entry · medium · "in apposition to boldāgendra" is impossible (genitive vs nominative); the participle stands in apposition to the subject hīe. Done: corrected.
- boldāgendra · entry · low · "partitive after hæleða" misdescribed the construction; it is in apposition to hæleða. Done: corrected.
- hildedīor · entry · low · "in apposition to byre"; it agrees with hæle. Done: corrected.
- burhwelan · entry · low · "probably accusative plural" contradicted l/i (singular "wealth") and the brūcan entry (genitive). Done: weak masculine, object of brūcan, genitive or accusative, case uncertain.
- īsernscūre · entry · low · "accusative singular" asserted a case the -e ending does not fit. Done: case marked uncertain.
- gegongen (broaden) · new reading · low · "of a hoard visited" pinned the entry to the line. Done: general wording with the phrase 'grimme gegongen'.
- lǣne (broaden) · new reading · low · "accusative singular masculine" for the form lǣne is not secure; the new reading now says "agreeing with dǣl, or adverbial". Done.
- gewearð (new broaden) · low · the known entry covers "came about, happened, was agreed" but not "became" with a past participle (wearð gewrecen). Done: " · geweorðan — became ... forming a passive".
- lȳt (new broaden) · medium · the known entry is a noun taking a genitive; in lȳt ǣnig mearn it is an adverb "hardly". Done: broadened.
- sēlestan (new broaden) · low · known entries list nominative plural, accusative singular and dative singular; þā sēlestan here is accusative plural. Done: broadened.
- wundur (new broaden) · low · known entry lists accusative singular or plural only; Wundur hwār is nominative singular. Done: broadened.
- wǣre (new broaden) · low · known entry lists "wǣr ... (accusative singular)"; on ðæs Waldendes wǣre is dative singular. Done: broadened.
